keySentence: Greed destroys more than it gives.

facts.Page story text 1 (draft, teacher check: The pirates wanted all the gold. They started to fight each other. Greed makes people selfish. Greed destroys more than it gives.
facts.Page story text 2 (draft, teacher check: The pirates only cared about gold and jewels. They forgot about friendship and promises. Greed made them suspicious of each other. They started arguing about who would get more treasure. Greed destroys more than it gives. Greed was destroying them from the inside.
facts.Page story text 3 (draft, teacher check: The pirates had launched their mutiny driven entirely by greed for the treasure. All they could think about was gold, silver, and precious jewels waiting to be found. In their obsession, they forgot every bond of friendship and loyalty they once had. Silver struggled to keep his men under control as they argued bitterly among themselves. Greed destroys more than it gives. However, the irony was that they had not even found the treasure yet. Because greed consumed their minds, they could not work together or think clearly. Their selfishness was slowly tearing the pirate group apart from within.
